outcome.technical: All in tools/check-git-pipeline.py (the only file). Requirement clauses: (1) 'the nt branch of _shim_dir and of the k15 working shim writes .cmd files' - both now come from pure functions _shim_spec / _passthrough_spec (file:2592, 2604) and one writer _write_shim (2612, newline='' so CRLF is written verbatim); _shim_dir (~2570) and k15 (in _interpreter_cases) both call them, so the nt spelling exists once. (2) 'a .cmd found by shutil.which and run without a shell is an assumption' - checked against the documentation and source, not memory: shutil.which reads PATHEXT from the PROCESS environment (os.getenv), not from the path argument, and falls back to a default list that carries .CMD (read in CPython v3.8.18 Lib/shutil.py and main; the repo floor is 3.8, CI runs 3.12); CPython main Doc/library/subprocess.rst line 458: 'You do not need shell=True to run a batch file', and line 770: batch files are launched by the OS in a system shell, arguments parsed by shell rules without Python escaping. So both assumptions are documented behaviour; what the docs cannot say is whether OUR bytes work, hence the Windows cases. (3) 'a cmd shim that forwards %* to sys.executable is an assumption' - k23 sends the exact probe interpreter_problem sends (-c with a space, semicolon, parentheses, quotes) through the forwarder and requires output 'ran'; k24 requires the exit code 5 of the target to come back. (4) 'Confirm on the first windows CI run' - cannot be done from this machine (darwin); not done, and said so: the cases are written to RUN on Windows and the owner commands are below. (5) 'If k13-k15 go red, build as .bat or add the extension to PATHEXT' - deliberately NOT applied pre-emptively: the sources show .CMD resolves even with PATHEXT unset, so a change would be a fix for a failure not observed. k21's label prints PATHEXT and the found path, k22 the codes, so a red names which of the remedies applies (PATHEXT/which -> add .CMD to os.environ PATHEXT in the case; k22 -> .bat or shell; k23 -> quoting). New cases: k18 (nt spec bytes: .cmd name, every LF is CRLF, exit code 7 not a fixed 1, forwarder quotes a target containing a space and keeps %*), k19 (posix spec unchanged: no extension, shebang, LF, exec ... "$@" - the other direction), k20 (_shim_dir writes one file per name, read back in binary equal to the spec for THIS platform - this one runs on Windows too and would show newline translation), all portable. k21-k24 run only on Windows (os.name == 'nt'); elsewhere they are ONE case printed 'k21-k24 SKIPPED HERE - ...' through _harness.skip (absent=True off nt), so it counts as a visible PASS line saying it was skipped; it cannot be mistaken for the real run. Evidence: python3 tools/check-git-pipeline.py --selftest on darwin -> ALL PASS 21/21 (was 17/17). Red first: before the implementation the selftest raised NameError _shim_spec ('SELFTEST FAILED: 17/18'). Mutations on a scratch copy, each restored, each red in the intended case: CRLF->LF in nt exit spec -> k18 only; nt extension .bat -> k18 only; posix shebang removed -> k13,k14,k19; _shim_dir writes only the first name -> k20 only; forwarder drops %* -> k18 only. The Windows-only logic of k21-k24 was exercised on darwin by a mirror (os.name faked to nt, posix shim specs): k22, k23, k24 true, k21 false only on the '.cmd' extension test, as it must be there. Full sweep: python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --quiet from the task tree, exit 0, '335/335 files ok, 153 migrated to tests/, 16640 cases'. Did not run capture-screenshots, check-report-interactive or verify.sh (orchestrator addendum). The plan gate refused my first attempt (a Bash heredoc writing the source file, 'change magnitude 119 > 80'); I stopped using Bash for it and made every edit with the Edit tool, which the gate allowed (the file is in the task's files). OWNER, WINDOWS (PowerShell), from a clone at the commit this lands on: `python tools\check-git-pipeline.py --selftest | Select-String -Pattern '^(PASS|FAIL) k(1[3-9]|2[0-4])|SKIPPED|ALL PASS|SELFTEST FAILED'; $LASTEXITCODE` (use `py` instead of `python` if python is not on PATH; takes about as long as the CI selftest leg for this file because k1 builds a real repository). PASS looks like: PASS k13, k14, k15, k17 (as before), PASS k16, PASS k18, PASS k19, PASS k20, PASS k21, PASS k22, PASS k23, PASS k24, no line containing 'SKIPPED', then 'ALL PASS: 24/24 cases passed' and $LASTEXITCODE 0 (on a non-Windows machine the same command prints one 'k21-k24 SKIPPED HERE' line and 21/21). FAIL looks like a line starting 'FAIL k21' / 'FAIL k22' / 'FAIL k23' / 'FAIL k24' (the detail is in the label: found path and PATHEXT for k21, exit codes for k22, found/code/output for k23, code for k24), 'SELFTEST FAILED: n/24', or any 'SKIPPED' line on Windows (that would mean the skip fired on the platform that has the mechanism). A red on k21-k24 means k13-k15 would be red on Windows CI for the same reason. Not verified and said plainly: a shim directory whose path contains a space (a Windows user name with a space in TEMP) - Windows launches a batch file via cmd with the original command line, and whether cmd's quote stripping survives a quoted .cmd path plus a quoted argument is not documented in what I read; the CI runner's TEMP has no space, so no case probes it.
outcome.descriptive: The Windows .cmd shims behind k13-k15 are built from one pure spec, pinned byte for byte on every platform (k18-k20), and a Windows-only block (k21-k24, a visible SKIPPED line elsewhere) now asks a real Windows machine whether PATHEXT lookup, list-argv execution, %* forwarding and exit codes behave.
